title: Conclusions and recommendations

blocks.heading: Conclusions and recommendations
blocks.text: A conclusion answers the question from findings within their limits; a recommendation proposes a feasible response tied to that answer and identifies an implementer. Do not introduce uncollected evidence. For community action distinguish aims, organisation, funding and implementation obstacles: assigning volunteers does not obtain money, and an obstacle needs a matched response and responsible actor.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Conclusion
blocks.text: A conclusion is an evidence-based answer to the research question or judgement about the hypothesis, within the enquiry’s limits. A sample pattern can support a bounded answer, not a claim about all places. Findings are the supporting observations, not interchangeable with the conclusion.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Recommendation
blocks.text: A recommendation is a proposed feasible action linked to the findings and conclusions, identifying who could implement it. Name the practical change, implementer and relevant resource condition. A wish such as “improve development” is too vague to follow.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: In an invented enquiry, repeated records show that a service opens late because a qualified operator arrives after the scheduled start. A feasible recommendation could revise staffing arrangements through the responsible provider. It addresses the observed obstacle more directly than an unrelated poster. State the evidence, responsible actor and resources, and distinguish a proposed response from one already carried out.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
blocks.repair_note: Codex targeted third-review repairs R3-01–R3-10; pre-repair snapshot retained in review/repairs/round3/.

blocks.heading: Organisation, funding and implementation
blocks.text: A fictional storage activity costing N$600 with N$200 available needs N$400 additional resources. Agreeing volunteers and dates organises it; recording contributions funds it. If a required lid is late, the coordinator should arrange a provider-approved suitable alternative or delay use. For a book project costing N$100 with N$40 available, seek N$60 or suitable in-kind materials and use the offered dry room to prevent the stated storage loss. These are project plans, not evidence that either was implemented. A recommendation identifies an implementer and follows findings; a conclusion does not introduce a new result.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Keep your own enquiry record
blocks.text: Keep an individual dated record with these fields: topic and study area; question or hypothesis; aim and specific objectives; dates and the defined population; sample size and actual selection procedure; consent and safety arrangements; instruments and pilot problem, revision and recheck; collection procedure; anonymised observations, units and missing values; table or graph with title and source; main findings and an exception; conclusion linked to the question; limitations; recommendation, implementer and required resources; actual researcher obstacle and response. Preserve changes and reasons. If working in a group, state what was shared and what you personally did. A missing stage should be marked not completed, rather than replaced by a fictional event. Use this record to answer Section B in your own words.
context_tags: Codex repair after independent review; original teaching synthesis

blocks.heading: Separate fictional demonstration from personal evidence
blocks.text: This demonstration is invented, not an enquiry you carried out. Suppose a safe observation found 12 visible items at one site and six at another during the same period, with one route inaccessible. The finding is a two-to-one count contrast in the observed places, not a result for the whole community. A conclusion can say the recorded sites differed, while noting missing coverage. A recommendation might ask the responsible collection provider to inspect the higher-count site. For your own answer, replace the demonstration with your actual observations and limits. Do not claim these counts, visits or recommendations as your own experience.
